title: Copper-Binding Peptides Attenuate Microglia Inflammation through Suppression of NF-kB Pathway.
authors: Caetano-Silva, Maria Elisa; Rund, Laurie A; Vailati-Riboni, Mario; Pacheco, Maria Teresa Bertoldo; Johnson, Rodney W
one_liner_zh: 该文研究乳清金属结合肽通过抑制NF-kB通路减轻小胶质细胞炎症，涉及肽与NF-kB p65的分子对接，但对象为肽-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: SCOPE: Activation of microglia, the resident immune cells of the central nervous system, has been related to the etiology and progression of neurodegenerative diseases; thus, finding novel approaches to suppress the neuroinflammatory process is of utmost relevance. METHODS AND RESULTS: The anti-inflammatory activity of whey Cu-, Fe-, and Zn-binding peptides and their possible underlying mechanism of action were evaluated in microglia. Whey metal-binding peptides decreased nitric oxide production and tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-alpha) at mRNA and protein levels by stimulated BV-2 microglia in comparison to the control with no peptide treatment. The hydrophobicity, specific sequences, and possible synergistic effects seem to play a role. Cu-binding peptides (Cu-bp) presented anti-inflammatory activity both in BV-2 and primary microglia cultures. These peptides exert their action by suppressing nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kB) pathway since nuclear translocation of NF-kB p65 is decreased by roughly 30% upon Cu-bp treatment. Specific sequences identified in Cu-bp showed high affinity to bind NF-kB p65 by molecular docking (up to -8.8 kcal mol(-1) ), corroborating the immunofluorescence studies. CONCLUSION: Cu-bp represent food-derived peptides that may be useful for neuroprotective purposes. Chelation of copper excess in the CNS and the bioavailability of such peptides, as well as their behavior in in vivo models, deserve further research for future applications.
abstract_zh: 范围：小胶质细胞作为中枢神经系统的常驻免疫细胞，其激活与神经退行性疾病的病因和进展相关；因此，寻找抑制神经炎症过程的新方法具有极其重要的意义。方法与结果：在小胶质细胞中评估了乳清铜、铁和锌结合肽的抗炎活性及其可能的潜在作用机制。与未接受肽处理的对照组相比，乳清金属结合肽降低了经刺激的BV-2小胶质细胞中一氧化氮的产生以及肿瘤坏死因子α（TNF-alpha）在mRNA和蛋白水平的表达。疏水性、特定序列及可能的协同效应似乎发挥作用。铜结合肽（Cu-bp）在BV-2和原代小胶质细胞培养中均表现出抗炎活性。这些肽通过抑制核因子κB（NF-kB）通路发挥作用，因为Cu-bp处理后，NF-kB p65的核转位减少了约30%。在Cu-bp中鉴定出的特定序列通过分子对接显示对NF-kB p65具有高结合亲和力（高达-8.8 kcal mol(-1)），这与免疫荧光研究结果相印证。结论：Cu-bp代表食物来源的肽，可能对神经保护目的有用。中枢神经系统中过量铜的螯合作用、此类肽的生物利用度及其在体内模型中的行为，值得进一步研究以供未来应用。
